newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul forward forex volume up 119 pct in first qtr.
newsitem.headline: Seoul forward forex volume up 119 pct in first qtr.

text.p: The average daily volume of South Korea's foreign exchange transactions in forward trading shot up 119 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997 after a rise in the won/dollar movement, the central bank said on Thursday.
A Bank of Korea (BOK) statement said the daily average of forward transactions reached $116 million in the three-month period from $53 million a year earlier.
"Foreign banks and domestic companies have expanded forward trading to hedge their possible foreign exchange risks following an expansion in the won/dollar movement," the statement said.
From February 1996, South Korea expanded the won/dollar daily fluctuation band to 2.25 percent on either side of the won's mid-rate to the U.S. dollar.
But dealers attributed the volume rise to the central bank's constant intervention, which the bank has never confirmed.

Dealers said the BOK repeatedly stepped into the foreign exchange market in the past months to slow a plunge in the local currency caused by a ballooning current account deficit and the strength of the dollar in the world market.
Average daily volume of overall interbank foreign exchange trading fell to $1.63 billion against $1.66 billion a year ago.
The spot transactions market comprised 93 percent of all foreign exchange trading during the first quarter against 98 percent a year ago, the statment said.
It said South Korea's won depreciated by 5.9 percent to 897.10 against the U.S. dollar at the end of March compared to 844.20 at the end of last year.
The local currency rose to 723.18 won per 100 yen at the end of March from 726.51 at the end of last year.
